paragraphs.text: Hello elders and sisters! All right, no new updates today, so let's just jump right into our discussion and review of this little book, Drawing on the Powers of Heaven by Grant von Harrison. As you recall from yesterday's podcast, I told you I would be doing a review, and the way we're going to handle this is that I will actually read the text from this little book, but interspersed in between readings, like I may read an idea or a paragraph or a couple of paragraphs, and then I'm going to have a little comment to share about that, where I'll make—maybe what I'll try to do is to expand on it a little bit, make sure that you have my insights on it as well. So there'll be a little bit of stopping and starting in the podcast, and you may notice that a little bit, but I don't think it'll be a problem.

So we're going to start with chapter one, which is entitled, The Nature and Function of Faith, and this is how it begins. Generally, members of the Church do not have difficulty understanding the most basic aspects of faith, such as faith that God lives, that Jesus is the Christ, that there is life after death, or with a general faith in the overall plan of salvation. However, many people do have trouble understanding the specific kind of faith required to draw on the powers of heaven to help them be more successful in every facet of their lives.

Regarding faith, the Prophet Joseph Smith taught that, number one, "as faith is the moving cause of all action in temporal concerns, so it is in spiritual." Two, "faith is not only the principle of action, but of power also." And three, "faith then is the first great governing principle which has power, dominion, and authority over all things."

Okay, now that's from the book. Now my thoughts on this, I found this to be true, that as you look at the members of the Church, we are a faith-filled people. It requires faith to be a member of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and we see broadly throughout the Church people of great faith. They believe in God, they believe in the Restoration, they believe in the Savior, they believe in the leadership of the Church. But we see also many members of the Church that don't have all the blessings they ought to have in their lives.

And what the author is saying, and I would agree, is that they have not learned how to use faith to draw down the powers of heaven for them personally. So yes, they believe in God. Yes, they have faith in all of these general things, but they have not learned how to use faith to change the circumstances of their life in a way that brings them more joy, more happiness, more success, and more ability to serve God in a more powerful way.

Back to the book. If you think about it, it is easy to see that faith is the moving cause of all action—exercising, planting a garden, studying for an examination. However, many members of the Church have trouble understanding the process required to experience what Joseph Smith referred to as the power that comes through faith. It is important that members of the Church understand that this power comes from faith in God, and they have to learn how to call upon this power, because without the powers of heaven, we are extremely limited in what we can accomplish in all aspects of our personal life. So members of the Church have power given them to do all things by faith, that's Second Nephi chapter 1, verse 10. By means of faith, as a principle of power, people accomplish or experience things they could not otherwise accomplish or experience.

We've seen this. We've seen this. We've seen this in people's lives where they exercise dramatic, remarkable, amazing faith, and they see miracles occur. You have seen it happen in your life. The question the author is asking us is why don't we see this in a more consistent and regular way? Why do we only use this process of faith in dramatic moments or moments of great alarm or moments of great focus? Why can't we use this process in a regular and consistent daily way in all the pursuits of our life?

Now let's talk about—back to the book. The function of faith, the author says. The following example illustrates the role of faith in motivating a person to action. If a man desires to lose 10 pounds, he must take the following steps. One, have faith in the laws that determine weight loss. Two, make a resolve to exercise daily and eat less. Three, maintain a constant effort motivated by faith.

Many people desire, however—rather I should say many desires cannot be realized by the faith that motivates us to action alone. There are many desires that require specific help from the Lord, in addition to resolve and determination on our part. For instance, a man becomes lost while hunting during a heavy snowstorm and he begins to pray that the Lord will preserve his life by inspiring him as to what direction he should go to find shelter or help. This desire will not be realized unless he is successful in calling down the powers of heaven to assist him.

Now I'm going to stop reading from the book for a second. As you look at these two examples, on the one hand with the man that wants to lose 10 pounds or—what's that about, 5 kilos, 4 kilos—he wants to lose that weight. In order for him to actually have the successful experience of losing the weight, he does have to exercise faith. But it's a different kind of faith. It's faith in the laws that determine weight loss. It's making that resolve to eat less and exercise a little more, and it's maintaining that effort, motivated by his faith that if he does so, he will achieve his goal.

On the other hand, you have the situation where someone's lost in the mountains—and I've been in that situation, we'll probably talk about that in a future podcast, but I've been in that situation—where you have to have the faith to call upon God to seek the powers of heaven to be exerted in your behalf in such a way that you can actually see things happen that you don't have the power to do for yourself. In other words, God intervenes in your behalf because of your faith.

Faith then—as this is back to the book—faith then as a principle of action involves resolve, decision making, and determination. Faith as a principle of power involves resolve, decision making, determination plus: one, belief in the Lord Jesus Christ; two, determination on the part of the individual to respond to the requirements of God; and three, bestowal of the powers of heaven, i.e., added strength, power, and force from God himself.

Okay, stepping away from the book for a second. What this is teaching us is there's two levels of faith. There's not two kinds of faith. There's two levels of faith. There is faith that drives us to action like the man who wants to lose the weight, but then there is faith that brings power. So that faith, which brings power, also brings action, but it goes beyond action and calls down power from heaven, power that we ourselves do not have. And we can only access it if we add to our resolve and decision making and determination these three things, which are belief in the Lord Jesus Christ, determination to do what we know we should be doing, i.e., the requirements of God keeping the commandments, and three, the ultimate bestowal of the power from heaven that gives us that added strength and force from God himself.

So back to the book, many righteous desires are very personal in nature and should be pursued through individual faith. However, there are some desires that warrant or require the collective faith of more than one person. When this is the case, you need to be very mindful of the faith or lack of faith of others.

Now, stepping away from the book, we've seen this in missionary work where one missionary in a companionship will be of great faith and the other missionary will not be of great faith. It is very difficult for that companionship to be able to bring about the powers of heaven because one member of the companionship is lacking in the collective or the individual faith that leads to the collective faith of the companionship. On the other hand, I have seen companionships where you have two missionaries, one's very, very experienced and very skillful, very knowledgeable, and of great faith. And the other one may be a brand new missionary who has very little skill, very little knowledge, no experience, but has great faith. And those two missionaries, through the exercise of that faith, the faith that drives action and power, can bring about miracles. We've seen it happen again and again and again.

But when the missionaries are divided in faith, nothing really good happens. They can be divided in experience. They can be divided in knowledge. They can be divided in skill. You can have one very skillful, one very knowledgeable, one very experienced, and one brand new missionary. But if their faith has a similar level of quality, those two missionaries will do miracles in the work.

Throughout the scriptures—this is back to the book—we see how the faith of the individual results in blessings for the masses. From the scriptures, we also learn, however, that there are exceptions to this. For example, when Mormon was called upon to be the military leader for the Nephites, his faith was a key factor in their success in battle. Yet the Nephites failed to see the hand of the Lord in their success and boasted of their own strength. Finally, Mormon's ability to exercise faith in their behalf was stifled or reduced.

Quote, "Behold, I had led them, notwithstanding their wickedness I had led them many times to battle, and had loved them, according to the love of God which was in me, with all my heart; and my soul had been poured out in prayer unto my God all the day long for them; nevertheless, it was without faith, because of the hardness of their hearts," close quote.

So back to the book. There are indeed many instances where the influences of the power of heaven requires collective faith. In the case of missionary work, the lack of faith of one companion can curtail the influence, reduce the influence of the Spirit when the missionaries are trying to teach a family. Likewise, the lack of faith on the part of several people can reduce the Spirit in a church meeting.

An individual missionary, ward leader, or whatever with great faith can draw upon the powers of heaven, but the process is increased or facilitated when more than one person lends faith to the same desired ends. When someone is ill, the group faith of all those associated with the blessing govern the powers of heaven. Obviously, great faith on the part of one person can have a tremendous effect when someone receives a blessing; in the final analysis, it is the combined faith or lack of faith of everyone associated with the blessing that determines whether or not the blessing is realized.

Now, away from the book for a second, let's think about this with relationship to our missionary work. As a mission, we have become a very successful mission, and we've remained that way even through the pandemic. And I think it's because we became a very collectively strong faith mission. We believed in our process, we believed in our purpose, but most importantly, we believed in God, and that we were doing the will of God. And that because we had paid the price to become very, very good at what we were doing, God would pave the way for us, clear the path for us, and allow us to achieve our goals, which is what allowed the mission to be so much more successful than so many other missions around the Philippines or around the world. It's faith that makes these things happen in the final analysis. You can be an exceptionally skilled missionary, but have no faith, and I can flat guarantee you, you will not bring about miracles.

Okay, back to the book. Once you become proficient at calling down the powers of heaven through faith, you should make every effort to teach others the process. If you work at it diligently, you will realize that you can be instrumental in teaching many others to be effective in calling down the powers of heaven. You will find that once others with whom you associate learn to exercise faith, the endeavors of the group will be sustained by the powers of heaven to a phenomenal degree. We've seen that in our mission.

The author goes on to say, in missions, stakes, wards, and families, where groups begin to exercise collective faith, the outpourings of the powers of heaven result in the lives of thousands of people being blessed. The most obvious indicator of collective faith is the number of people joining the Church in a given area. Collective faith is the key to the realization of President Spencer W. Kimball's desire to see millions of people join the Church each year.

Once the collective faith of the Church is sufficient, millions will join the Church each year, and the prophecies referring to the Church rolling forth as a stone and encompassing the entire earth will be fulfilled. As members of the Church, we need to realize that the fulfillment of these prophecies is contingent on the collective faith of the members of the Church. You will find it much easier to exercise faith when your faith is sustained by the faith of others, as is the case with physical tasks.

For instance, if you're trying to lift a heavy object or push a car, you can't do it by yourself, but when a group of people get together and work together, suddenly combining their physical strength, now you can push that car along quite easily; so it is with many righteous desires that require the collective faith or combined faith of many people.

Now, there's a diagram which I'm going to try to describe, but as soon as I'm done with the podcast, I will upload a picture of this diagram so that you can take a look at it. The following diagram depicts the process when someone is converted through the powers of faith and prayer. All right, what you see are several people exercising—in the words of Joseph Smith—using mental exertion, i.e. faith, towards God and asking for the powers of heaven to be drawn down from God on the person who is in the process of receiving the gospel.

So you see these people on one side of the page exercising their faith, exercising their mental exertion, and the arrow moving up towards the Father and the Son, and then on the other side of the page, the arrow moving down from the Father and the Son onto the person who is the recipient of the powers of heaven to receive answers to prayer, to know that the gospel is true, and so forth. Like I say, I will send this to you right after I've uploaded the podcast.

So number one, belief in the living God and the Lord Jesus Christ. Number two, determination to respond to the requirements of God, i.e. righteous living, following the counsel of the prophet, friending the people, etc. And three, faith in the power of God at your disposal. When you have those things, you create that flowchart which I'm going to send you a copy of.

Now the first time you read—or in your case listen to—this book, answer the following questions on a piece of paper. I want you to do this exercise. Answer these questions. Explain what is meant by the powers of heaven. Second question, how does the faith required to lose 10 pounds differ from the faith required to see someone converted through the power and faith of prayer? And as an added element, discuss your answers with your companion or your kabahays who are also listening to this.

All right, that sums up chapter one and we've got it done in less than 20 minutes. I'm excited to review this with you. I hope that you're learning from it and again, as I said, I love you. We're excited to serve with you. Let's build our faith and see the work even get bigger. Have a good night.
